title: Spin relaxation in $X$-wave magnets with $X=p, d, f, g, i$
authors: Lijie Liu, Mingbo Dou, Xu Chen, Xianjie Wang, M. Ye. Zhuravlev, A. V. Nikolaev, L. L. Tao
abstract: Spin relaxation results in the spin decoherence and a finite spin lifetime, which are detrimental to spintronic devices. To achieve a long spin lifetime desirable for spintronic devices, elucidating the spin relaxation mechanism and factors influencing the spin lifetime is of vital importance. Here, we investigate the spin relaxation in $X$-wave magnets ($X=p, d, f, g, i$) with Rashba spin-orbit coupling within the framework of D'yakonov-Perel' mechanism. We calculate the general matrix of the spin relaxation time for an arbitrary Néel vector direction of the $X$-wave magnet. As an illustration, we study the spin relaxation for the Néel vector along the $[001]$ direction. It is found that the reciprocal spin-relaxation-time matrices are anisotropic and diagonal for the $d$-, $f$-, $g$- and $i$-wave magnets. For the $p$-wave magnet, we derive the analytical expressions for the temporal evolution of spins. Moreover, the spin relaxation rate is proportional to the momentum relaxation time, Rashba and altermagnetic spin-split strengths for all $X$-wave magnets. Our results shine more light on the fundamental understanding of the spin relaxation mechanism in $X$-wave magnets.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates spin relaxation in various types of X-wave magnets ($p, d, f, g, i$) relevant to spintronics. Using the D'yakonov-Perel' mechanism, the authors calculate the spin decoherence rates, finding distinct symmetry behaviors across different wave symmetries. The results provide a deeper understanding of how material structure dictates spin lifetime in these advanced magnetic systems.
main_problem: The study investigates spin relaxation mechanisms, which cause spin decoherence and limit the spin lifetime in spintronic devices.
main_result: The authors found that for $d$-, $f$-, $g$-, and $i$-wave magnets, the reciprocal spin-relaxation-time matrices are anisotropic and diagonal when the Néel vector is along [001].
method: The analysis employs the D'yakonov-Perel' mechanism within a kinetic equation framework, solving for the tensor of reciprocal spin relaxation times.
model_or_system: The system models 2D $X$-wave magnets ($p, d, f, g, i$) incorporating Rashba spin-orbit coupling and an effective Zeeman term. The dynamics are governed by a kinetic equation derived from Boltzmann transport theory.
key_observables: The tensor of reciprocal spin relaxation times (1/tau_ij) and the temporal evolution of the averaged spin vector S(t).
important_parameters: Rashba SOC strength ($\alpha$), momentum relaxation time ($	au$), and altermagnetic spin-split strengths ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the $q=0$ limit, describing uniform distribution and coherent precession; it also assumes a specific Néel vector direction for initial calculations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows Fermi contours for the five wave types, indicating node lines where spin splitting vanishes. Figure 2 illustrates the temporal decay of spin components for the $p$-wave magnet.
paper_structure: The paper systematically calculates the general matrix form of the relaxation tensor ($D_{SO}$), applies this to specific symmetry cases ($d, f, g, i$ vs. $p$), derives explicit time evolution solutions for the $p$-wave case, and concludes with detailed calculations for correlation functions in $g$- and $i$-wave magnets.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental theoretical insights into spin relaxation dynamics in novel magnetic materials using advanced transport theory, which is crucial for designing next-generation spintronic devices.
